newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African funds unfazed by Wall Street falls.
newsitem.headline: S.African funds unfazed by Wall Street falls.

text.p: South African fund managers said they had largely anticipated the current weakness on Wall Street by reducing their equity exposure in favour of cash.

Fund managers told Reuters they had gone light on equities in the United States and other major markets in anticipation of a correction, but had not significantly altered their asset distribution in South Africa.
Wall Street recorded its worst falls since August 1990 on Thursday and Monday with back-to-back losses totalling nearly 300 points on the blue-chip Dow index.

Adrian Allardice, senior portfolio manager at Old Mutual Asset Managers, the country's biggest investment institution with 198 billion rand ($44.9 billion) under management, said U.S. equities had appeared overvalued for some time.
"In our international assets, we have taken underweight positions in America... and in some other major markets to offset some of the areas of concern," he said.
"If a market is overvalued, we'll be underweight there.
"We have been reducing holdings in markets that have been running very strongly and moving to more peripheral markets in Europe that look good - Italy, Scandinavia and the like," he said.

Allardice said he had recently taken hedge positions in the company's key Profile range of pension and employee-benefit funds to protect assets against a negative effect of the recent 0.25 percentage point U.S. interest rate hike.
Charl le Roux, executive director of Sanlam Asset Management, said he was relieved about the correction on Wall Street and did not anticipate any major additional movement.
"We knew that a correction was on the cards. We have known that one risk factor was the overvalued U.S. market. We're a lot happier now," he said.

Board of Executors portfolio manager Rene du Plessis said her company had been relatively underweight on equities in South Africa prior to Thursday's fall and would use the correction as an opportunity to buy.
"We were in the low to mid-60s on equities while most of our competitors were probably closer to 70 percent so we'll use this as an opportunity to correct that," she said.

Charles Foster, a senior mutual fund portfolio manager at Momentum Life, said he had increased liquidity ahead of the weekend fall and probably would stay well over 10 percent in cash for the immediate future.
"We felt that for quite a long period there had been a lot of risk, that equities had been highly priced and that there would be a correction," he said.
"We're still wary. There's still a lot of volatility," he said.
-- Cape Town newsroom +27 21 252238 ($ = 4.41 South African Rand)
